quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power can the front brake provide?
questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 75 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should a pre-ride inspection do?

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only take a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A proper inspection takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to your following distance during the day?

options.text: Allow a longer following distance at night.
Allow a shorter following distance at night.
Keep the same following distance day or night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances because you cannot see shadows and light contrasts. Increase your following distance when riding at night.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you very closely.
Look only at your controls, not ahead.
Let other drivers know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know your plans.
questions.explanation: Help prevent crashes by making yourself visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show what you plan to do. Keep space around your motorcycle and always look ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They are caused by bald tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve new riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of riding experience. Most crashes happen during the day at low speeds.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you will slow down quickly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down quickly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as bright as a car's. Flash your brake light when you need to slow down faster than drivers expect. This helps them notice you.

questions.question: When turning left, what should you do?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean that way.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all crashes?

options.text: They are caused by worn tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who are inexperienced on their motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden moves. Stay away from the road edge and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up to put distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things more dangerous.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around their motorcycle.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions are always changing, so the safest lane position changes too. Choose the position that gives you the most space around your motorcycle and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: When selecting a helmet, make sure it has all of the following qualities, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Looks attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that tell drivers about rules, like speed limits, are rectangular. They have white backgrounds with black lettering or symbols. Riders must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without forcing inexperienced riders to lead.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Use your high beam headlight when safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes at night, reduce your speed and increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Use the headlights of vehicles in front of you to see farther ahead. Use your high beam headlight, except when you are following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: When another vehicle is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get ahead of you. If you can do so safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make the danger worse by encouraging them to tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of being in a crash, you should:

options.text: Not use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Watch only about five feet ahead of your motorcycle while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Use your turn signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you. Always be ready to avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
Give you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps safety in many ways. It keeps you out of other vehicles' blind spots, helps you see and be seen better, helps you avoid road hazards, helps you avoid wind from other vehicles, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself in a way that discourages other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder.
Look over your shoulder and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you change lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, riders under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets. Passengers should wear tight clothing to avoid getting caught on the motorcycle and should lean with the rider during turns. Never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of a motorcycle's braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
Should only be used when the road is wet.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face, including your eyes. Goggles protect only your eyes, not your face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield should be all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Airtight.
questions.explanation: Eye protection and face shields should be free of scratches, resistant to breaking through, have clear side vision, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses.
